evidence.limits: Machine transcript checked against my frame reading after first coding. It mishears names ('יל גולן', 'אליי') and a few words; burned-in captions used for exact wording. Sound effects not determinable. Comment category counts are my own approximate hand count over 44 sampled comments. Speech fields checked against the transcript on 09 Nov 2026 (text-only pass).

topic_detail: Popularity is not quality: the 'best singer' or 'best chef' is just whoever you see most; the same brain link makes followers social proof, and in his club example about 300,000 viewers led to 3,000 buyers (1 percent), a group he says is worth about 85 million; non-buyers pay in 'another currency': attention.
audience: aspiring business owners and creators who sell with social media
caption_vs_video_note: Caption is a long written essay on attention as the new currency and posting daily; the video is a stage lecture on how popularity is mistaken for quality and the 1 percent who buy. Same theme (social proof from followers), different framing: caption includes advice on daily posting and controversy which is not heard in the frames I could read.

t=49-56 s: slower while he writes the numbers on the flipchart
t=60-90 s: sentence-length shots with a few light-leak transitions
editing.ending: He stands in front of the audience; captions 'אנשים שצופים בכם ולא יקנו! אבל אתם רוצים אותם! במטבע אחר: תשומת לב בצפיות' (about 1:21-1:28.5, from sampled captions).
editing.rewatch_reasons: interpretation: long for a Reel (90 s) and information-dense, with a closing line that restates the core idea; shareable (519 shares) more than commented.

text.language: Rhetorical questions and short punch phrases, concrete names; 'מי הזמר הכי טוב?'
text.caption_structure: Long essay: first line 'המטבע החדש ב2025 הוא תשומת לב', claims '99% מהעוקבים שלכם לא יקנו מכם', advice to post daily and take positions; ends 'אין דבר כזה שיווק רע'. No CTA, no hashtags.
text.rtl_notes: Hebrew punctuation is placed correctly on screen; digits and % render in the right order ('1%').

story.setup: Who is the best singer in the country? Audience guesses Eyal Golan, Omer Adam.
story.stakes: Being the most heard is not the same as being the best, yet people confuse the two.
story.progression: Singer, then best chef (TV), then 'whoever is best in the field', then the club's numbers: 300,000 viewers, 3,000 buyers, 1%.
story.payoff: Followers are social proof; the 1 percent who buy (3,000 of 300,000, said to be worth about 85 million, machine transcript) matter; attention in views is the 'other currency'.
story.resolution: Closing line about people watching you who will not buy, but you want them, with attention in views as the currency.
story.payoff_delivered: yes: the 1% numbers example and the closing summary
friction_points: t=60-90 s: the second half repeats the 1% point with fewer visual changes (interpretation)
t=45 s: split screen with a small speaker on the lower half makes the captions overlap the picture (interpretation)

engagement.comment_notes: Approximate hand count over the 44 sampled comments. The sample is dominated by debate over who is the best singer ('אייל גולן הזמר הכי טוב', 'לא נכון', 'כמה שטויות בסרטון אחד'), alongside praise ('מסר מדהים'). Not representative of all 319 comments.
engagement.creator_reply_pattern: Emoji or tag acknowledgments to accounts (a fire emoji, a raised-hands emoji); no argument seen.

rights_and_privacy: Third-party content: a photo of Eyal Golan with awards and a concert clip of a singer, a photo of a man and woman, a photo of three chefs and a television-style chef clip. Audience members, including a woman at 30 s, are identifiable; no minors identified.
why_it_may_work: Interpretation: the opening question with a named, famous example gets quick participation, and the hard numbers on the flipchart turn an abstract idea into a concrete 300,000-to-3,000 lesson; the debate in comments adds engagement.
why_it_may_underperform: Interpretation: at 90 s the second half restates the point, and the topic needs prior marketing interest.

standout_moments.what: Question 'מי הזמר הכי טוב במדינה?' answered within 2 s with named stars and a cut to the packed hall.
Red-circled 300,000 on the flipchart, then 3,000 and 1%: the central number moment.
Closing line connects attention to a currency, matching the caption.
